office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: Optional: may replace up to 50% of the water closets (New Mexico sentence in Section 2902.1)
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.urinals: Optional: may replace up to 67% of the water closets (A occupancy; New Mexico sentence in Section 2902.1)
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200

school.urinals: Optional: may replace up to 67% of the water closets (E occupancy; New Mexico sentence in Section 2902.1)

sex_split.text: Half the occupant load is counted as male and half as female, unless approved statistical data show another split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 2902.1. ... Exceptions: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number. In a building with several occupancies, the fractions are added first and then rounded up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. New Mexico's own sentence lets them replace up to 50% of the toilets in offices and other non-assembly, non-school uses, and up to 67% in assembly (restaurants) and educational occupancies. The sentence says 'maximum number of water closets' and does not say how to round the percentage; the worked examples apply it to the required number and round down.
urinal_substitution.quote: urinals may be substituted for up to fifty percent of the maximum number of water closets in other than A or E occupancies; in A and E occupancies, urinals may be substituted for up to sixty-seven percent of the maximum number of water closets.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Not settled by the state rule. In the model code the rule on separate rooms for each sex and its small-occupancy exceptions (15 or fewer people in any use, 25 or fewer in an office, 100 or fewer in a store) sit in IBC Section 2902.2. New Mexico's rule deletes Chapter 29 except Section 2901, Section 2902.1, Table 2902.1 and Section 2902.1.1, so Section 2902.2 is not among the sections kept, and the 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code deletes the Uniform Plumbing Code's own separate-facilities section (422.2). UpCodes' copy of the New Mexico code still prints Section 2902.2 with the model exceptions. Ask CID (or the local building department) whether a small business may have one shared restroom.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 14.7.2.37 CHAPTER 29 - PLUMBING SYSTEMS: Delete this chapter of the IBC and see the NMPC except as provided below. | 2021 NMPC: (2) 422.2 Separate facilities. Delete this section of the UPC. | Model text shown on UpCodes: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. ... Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: IBC Table 1004.5, which New Mexico amends only by adding a line for correctional facilities: office (business areas) 150 gross sq ft per occupant; restaurant dining room (assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated, tables and chairs) 15 net sq ft; classroom 20 net sq ft.
occupant_load.quote: Assembly without fixed seats ... Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net ... Business areas 150 gross ... Educational Classroom area 20 net
occupant_load.state_amendment_quote: Table 1004.5 - Maximum floor area allowances per occupant. See this table of the IBC and amend as follows: under the function of space column, in the institutional areas block, below sleeping areas add: "correctional facilities and detention centers: 60 square feet gross floor area per occupant".

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals: 50% of 1 = 0.5, rounded down to 0.
100 each. First 50: 50/25 = 2; remaining 50: 50/50 = 1; total 3 each. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, rounded down to 1.
200 each. First 50: 2; remaining 150: 150/50 = 3; total 5 each. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, rounded down to 2.
25 each. 25/75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, rounded down to 0.
50 each. 50/75 = 0.67, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, rounded down to 0.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2 each. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, rounded down to 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3 each. Urinals: 67% of 3 = 2.01, rounded down to 2.
25 each. 25/50 = 0.5, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, rounded down to 0.
50 each. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, rounded down to 0.
100 each. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, rounded down to 1.
200 each. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals: 67% of 4 = 2.68, rounded down to 2.

access.state_standard: Chapter 11 of the 2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code (14.7.2.19 NMAC: IBC Chapter 11 with state amendments), IBC Appendix E as amended (14.7.2.44 NMAC, with New Mexico's Table E111 for children's elements), and 'the current adopted ICC A117.1'. The rule cites ANSI A117.1-2017 in Table E111 and in 14.7.2.45, and the 2021 IBC references the 2017 edition. The federal 2010 ADA Standards apply alongside.
access.state_standard_quote: Section 1102.1 Design. Delete this section of the IBC except and substitute with the following: Building and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with this chapter, Appendix E - Supplementary Accessibility Requirements, and the current adopted ICC A117.1.

differences.point: Two accessible fixtures in very large restrooms (New Mexico's own amendment)
differences.state: When a restroom has 20 or more fixtures of one type, at least two of that type must be accessible.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 213.3.1: 'Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1.'
differences.quote: Section 1110.2 - Toilet and bathing facilities. ... Insert the following sentence at the end of the first paragraph: When 20 or more fixtures of any type are installed in an accessible toilet room or bathing room, at least two of that type shall be accessible.

differences.point: Share of wheelchair and ambulatory stalls
differences.state: IBC 1110.2.4 (unamended): at least 5% of the compartments in a toilet room must be wheelchair accessible, and where compartments plus urinals total six or more, at least 5% must be ambulatory accessible in addition.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 213.3.1: 'Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition to the compartment required to comply with 604.8.1, at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.'
differences.quote: 1110.2.4 Water Closet Compartment Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.
differences.note: The difference only bites above 20 compartments in one room. Read on UpCodes (secondary).

differences.point: Vertical grab bar on the side wall
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2017 604.5.1 requires a vertical grab bar, 18 inches minimum, in addition to the horizontal side-wall bar.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: 'The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.' No vertical bar.
differences.quote: 604.5.1 Fixed Side-Wall Grab Bars Fixed side-wall grab bars shall include a horizontal bar complying with Section 604.5.1.1 and a vertical grab bar complying with Section 604.5.1.2. ... 604.5.1.2 Vertical Grab Bar A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor
differences.note: Read on UpCodes' copy of ICC A117.1-2017 under New Mexico (secondary).

differences.point: Toe clearance under the partitions of a wheelchair stall
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2017 604.9.5.1: 12 inches high and 8 inches deep. The exemption sizes are also larger: no front toe clearance needed only in a stall deeper than 64 inches (wall-hung toilet) or 67 inches (floor-mounted); no side toe clearance only in a stall wider than 68 inches.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.4: 'The front partition and at least one side partition shall provide a toe clearance of 9 inches (230 mm) minimum above the finish floor and 6 inches (150 mm) deep minimum beyond the compartment-side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members.' Exemption above 62 inches deep (wall-hung) or 65 inches (floor-mounted), and above 66 inches wide.
differences.quote: 604.9.5.1 Toe Clearance at Wheelchair Accessible Toilet Compartments The front partition and at least one side partition of wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members. Exceptions: Toe clearance at the front partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 64 inches (1625 mm) in depth with a wall-hung water closet, or greater than 67 inches (1700 mm) in depth with a floor-mounted water closet. Toe clearance at the side partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 68 inches (1725 mm) in width.

differences.point: Children's stalls are mandatory where children are the main users
differences.state: New Mexico's Appendix E says children's dimensions 'shall be applied' where children are the primary users (day care centers, schools, children's areas of libraries), and its Table E111 gives the sizes by age group: wheelchair stall 60 inches wide by 59 inches deep, 12-inch toe clearance, ambulatory stall 60 inches long by 35 inches wide, plus toilet centerline, seat and grab bar heights for ages 3-4, 5-8 and 9-12.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.4: 'Compartments for children's use shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the finish floor.' The federal children's provisions apply when a compartment is built for children's use; this quote is the only federal children's text read.
differences.quote: E112.1. The predominant use of an element (rather than a building or facility) shall guide the determination of whether to use specifications for adults or children for that element. If children are the primary users of the element, children's specifications shall be applied. ... E112.2 - Children's Accessible Elements. When children are the primary users of a building or facility (such as day care centers, schools, children's areas of libraries, etc.), the accessibility standards shall correspond to the children's provisions of this section.

differences.point: Baby changing station in new public restrooms (state law, not a stall rule)
differences.state: A new restroom in a place of public accommodation must have at least one baby changing facility on each floor that has a public toilet, usable by any person.
differences.federal: No federal requirement to provide one.
differences.quote: 14.7.2.45 BABY CHANGING FACILITIES A. Construction of a new restroom, intended for use in a place of public accommodation, as defined in 14.5.2 NMAC, shall provide for at least one baby changing facility on each floor that has a public toilet facility and shall accommodate any person needing to utilize a baby changing facility, pursuant to Section 60-13-10.3 NMSA 1978.

access.process: No separate state accessibility registration or review step appears in 14.7.2 NMAC (nothing like a registered accessibility specialist). Accessibility is checked in ordinary plan review and inspection by the Construction Industries Division or the local building department; the rule says baby changing facilities must be on the submitted plans and are subject to plan review and inspection before a certificate of occupancy. Not read: whether the Governor's Commission on Disability reviews plans.

single_user.rule: Gender-Free Restrooms Act (Laws 2019, HB 388; cited in search results as NMSA 1978, Sections 28-24-1 to 28-24-3): a single-user toilet facility in a public accommodation, existing or built on or after July 1, 2019, must be open to any person regardless of gender identity or sex, be for one occupant at a time or for family or assisted use, and carry gender-neutral signage. It does not require building one where none exists. The model building code sentence (IBC 2902.1.2) says the same about signs, but that section is not among those New Mexico's rule keeps.
single_user.quote: SECTION 3. PUBLIC FACILITY AVAILABILITY.-- A. A single-user toilet facility that exists or is constructed on or after July 1, 2019 in a public accommodation shall be: (1) made available to any person regardless of gender identity or sex; (2) designated for use by not more than one occupant at a time or for family or assisted use; and (3) identified with gender-neutral signage. B. Nothing in this section shall be construed to require construction of a new, single-user toilet facility if one does not exist in a public accommodation.
single_user.definitions_quote: "gender-neutral signage" means a sign that indicates a restroom without preference or distinction to a specific gender identity or sex; ... "single-user toilet facility" means a single-occupancy restroom with an outer door that can be locked by the occupant.

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed. The fixture-calculation section New Mexico keeps (IBC 2902.1.1, exception 2) provides for multiple-user rooms designed to serve all genders: the count is worked out on the whole occupant load, each fixture type must meet ICC A117.1, and every urinal must be in a stall. The model code's companion rule on toilet privacy (IBC 2902.2 exception 6) is not among the sections New Mexico's rule keeps, so the state text does not spell out the stall construction.
all_gender_shared.quote: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.
all_gender_shared.adoption_quote: (2) Section 2902.1.1 - Fixture Calculations. See this section of the IBC.

use_restrictions.rule: None found. No New Mexico statute restricting restroom use by sex in public buildings was found. The Human Rights Act (NMSA 1978, Section 28-1-7(F), as amended by Laws 2023, HB 207) bars public accommodations, which since 2023 include governmental entities, from making a distinction in offering their facilities because of sex or gender identity.
use_restrictions.quote: F. any person in any public accommodation to make a distinction, directly or indirectly, in offering or refusing to offer its services, facilities, accommodations or goods to any person because of race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, pregnancy, childbirth or condition related to pregnancy or childbirth, spousal affiliation or physical ... | H. "public accommodation" means any governmental entity or any establishment that provides or offers its services, facilities, accommodations or goods to the public, but does not include a bona fide private club or other place

restrooms.confidence_note: Both acts were read as enrolled bills on nmlegis.gov (official), not in the compiled statutes (nmonesource.com not opened). 'None found' for restrictions rests on the search done, not on a complete review of the statutes.

public_wage.law: Public Works Minimum Wage Act, NMSA 1978, Sections 13-4-11 to 13-4-17; rules at 11.1.2 NMAC
public_wage.threshold: Contracts or projects over $60,000 to which the state or a political subdivision is a party
public_wage.who_sets: The director of the Labor Relations Division, New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, sets the rates each year after a public hearing and publishes them in 11.1.2.20 NMAC. Building work is 'Type B: General Building'.
public_wage.rates_note: The State Records Center copy of 11.1.2.20 NMAC read on 2026-11-24 still showed the 2025 rates (Type B, Carpenter/lather: base 30.89, fringe 13.26, apprenticeship .60; Los Alamos county 37.39 / 14.18 / .60). The 2026 rates are on the Department's Public Works page (https://www.dws.nm.gov/Public-Works), which rejected automated access. The city agent must take the Bernalillo County rate from the current schedule.
public_wage.quote: Every contract or project in excess of $60,000 that the state or any political subdivision thereof is a party to for construction, alteration, demolition or repair or any combination of these, including painting and decorating, of public buildings, public works or public roads of the state and that requires or involves the employment of mechanics, laborers or both shall contain a provision stating the minimum wages and fringe benefits to be paid to various classes of laborers and mechanics, which shall be based upon the wages and benefits that will be determined by the director to be prevailing for the corresponding classes of laborers and mechanics employed on contract work of a similar nature in the state or locality
public_wage.quote_2: The director shall: (1) coordinate the administration of the Public Works Minimum Wage Act; (2) annually determine the prevailing wage and fringe benefit rates and the rate for the employer contributions to the public works apprentice and training funds, and publish said rates;
public_wage.confidence_note: Threshold and rate-setting read in the official rule (11.1.2.8 and 11.1.2.9 NMAC). The statute itself (Section 13-4-11) was not opened: Justia returned 403 and nmonesource.com was not tried.

sales_tax.tax_name: Gross receipts tax (GRT). New Mexico has no sales tax: the tax is on the seller's or contractor's receipts and is usually passed on to the customer as a separate line. The buyer's counterpart is the compensating tax.
sales_tax.state_rate_quote: The gross receipts tax rate varies throughout the state from 4.875% to 10.8125%. ... The state's portion of the gross receipts tax (4.875%), which is also the largest portion of the tax, is determined by state law. Changes to the state rate occur no more than once a year, usually in July.
sales_tax.state_rate_note: From FYI-105 as posted on 2026-11-24, whose cover reads 'July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026'. Confirm no change took effect July 1, 2026. The city agent takes the combined Albuquerque rate from the Department's rate schedule.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. An out-of-state seller with no physical presence owes gross receipts tax on sales delivered into New Mexico once it had at least $100,000 of taxable New Mexico receipts in the previous calendar year; the rate is that of the delivery address. If the seller does not charge the tax, the buyer owes compensating tax at the state rate of 4.875% plus any local option. A sale of partitions to a contractor who gives the seller a nontaxable transaction certificate (Type 6, materials that become part of a construction project) is deductible, and the tax is then paid on the contractor's receipts.
shipped_goods.quote: For an individual or business that lacks physical presence in this state, including a marketplace provider or marketplace seller, engaging in business means having at least $100,000 of taxable gross receipts in the previous calendar year from sales, leases, and licenses of tangible personal property, sales of licenses, and sales of services or licenses for use of real property, sourced to New Mexico (Section 7-9-3.3 NMSA 1978). (FYI-206) | b. if the property is not received by the purchaser at the location of the seller, the location indicated by instructions for delivery to the purchaser, or the purchaser's donee, when known to the seller; (FYI-105) | Property that was acquired inside or outside New Mexico that would have been subject to gross receipts tax, but gross receipts tax was not charged in the purchase. (7-9-7). ... Compensating tax at a state rate of 4.875% plus any local option imposed. (FYI-105)

freight.rule: Delivery and freight charges the seller pays and passes on to the buyer are part of the taxable sale price. Freight the buyer pays directly to the carrier is not. Compensating tax likewise covers freight, delivery and handling billed by the seller.
freight.quote: C. Delivery expenses: (1) Receipts from charges by a seller of tangible personal property for delivery costs, including postage and transportation charges, paid by the seller and passed on to the buyer, are an element of the sales price of the property. ... D. Freight charges: (1) Transportation costs that are paid by the seller to the carrier are an element of the sales price of the property. (2) Transportation costs that are paid to the carrier by the buyer are not an element of the sales price of the property. (3.2.1.15 NMAC) | X must pay compensating tax on the value of these products, plus any freight, delivery and handling charges billed by the seller in New Jersey. (FYI-105)

install_labor.rule: Taxable. Gross receipts tax applies to receipts from performing services in New Mexico, and 'service' includes construction activities, so installation labor is taxed whether or not it is billed separately. Construction services are reported at the rate of the construction site. A subcontractor's labor sold to a contractor is deductible (the general contractor then pays the tax on the whole job).
install_labor.quote: Service includes construction activities and all construction materials that will become part of the construction project. (FYI-105) | If the gross receipts are from construction services and construction-related services, as those terms are defined under the Gross Receipts and Compensating Tax Act, performed for a construction project in New Mexico, the reporting location of the gross receipts and related deductions is the location of the construction site. (FYI-200)

furnish_and_install.rule: The contractor's whole receipts, labor and materials together, are taxed as a construction service at the job site's rate. The contractor can buy the materials without tax by giving the supplier a Type 6 nontaxable transaction certificate, because the finished project is taxed. Whether a partition installation on its own counts as 'construction' under the Act was not read; the outcome for the customer is the same, since both services and goods are taxed.
furnish_and_install.quote: "Service" includes construction activities and all tangible personal property that will become an ingredient or component part of a construction project. That tangible personal property retains its character as tangible personal property until it is installed as an ingredient or component part of a construction project in New Mexico. Sales of tangible personal property that will become an ingredient or component part of a construction project to persons engaged in the construction business are sales of tangible personal property; (Section 7-9-3 NMSA 1978 as quoted in FYI-200) | 1. Receipts from the sale of tangible personal property to a person in the construction business (7-9-51). Requirement: the tangible personal property by design and intent must become part of a construction project ... Requirement: upon its completion the construction project must be subject to gross receipts tax. ... NTTC Requirement: Type 6. (FYI-105)

sales_tax.pass_through_quote: Gross receipts tax (GRT) is imposed on businesses, but it is common for a business to pass the GRT on to the purchaser. If GRT is passed on to the customer, it is required to be separately stated on the invoice.
sales_tax.agency: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department

page.stalls_intro: New Mexico's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: they may replace up to half of the men's toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, so you can buy fewer men's stalls and add urinal screens.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. New Mexico's rules don't say clearly whether a small business may have one shared restroom, so ask your building department.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** New Mexico's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law and New Mexico's own building rules set the sizes, and the building department checks them when it reviews the plans.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **New Mexico extras:** stalls here need a second, upright grab bar on the side wall, and a wheelchair stall needs more toe room under its partitions (12 inches high, against 9 under the federal rules). A restroom with 20 or more toilets needs two accessible ones. Where children are the main users, as in a school or day care, the stalls must be built to children's sizes. A new public restroom needs a baby changing station on each floor that has one.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** state law requires a one-person restroom in a place open to the public to be available to anyone and marked with a gender-neutral sign. A shared all-gender room is allowed: the toilets are then counted for everyone in the building together, and every urinal must be in a stall.
page.public_jobs: On state, city, county and school projects over $60,000, New Mexico law requires at least the wage and benefits the state sets each year for each trade.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** New Mexico has a gross receipts tax in place of a sales tax, and it covers services. Installation labor is taxed, even when it's billed separately, at the rate of the job site. On a supply-and-install contract the contractor's whole price is taxed.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable, including freight billed by the seller. If the seller doesn't charge the tax, the buyer owes the matching compensating tax to the state.

sources: - Toilet counts and urinals: [14.7.2 NMAC, 2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.007.0002.html), section 14.7.2.37 (Table 2902.1 and Sections 2902.1 and 2902.1.1 of the 2021 International Building Code, with New Mexico's urinal sentence); the table rows were read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/new_mexico/ibc-2021/chapter/29/plumbing-systems). The plumbing code points there: [14.8.2 NMAC, 2024 New Mexico Plumbing Code](https://prod-rf-lambda.rtssaas.com/PublicFiles/d89c47bd0d70402dba89b03a22bda6d1/2ac74bd8-96b7-401a-a811-a4b33b04aa9e/14.008.0002.html), section 14.8.2.12, listed on the [Construction Industries Division's codes page](https://www.rld.nm.gov/construction-industries/rules-laws-and-building-codes/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Building capacity: Table 1004.5 of the 2021 International Building Code as adopted by [14.7.2.18 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.007.0002.html), read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/new_mexico/ibc-2021/chapter/10/means-of-egress). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Fire test for solid plastic partitions: Section 803.9 of the 2021 International Building Code (NFPA 286), adopted without change by [14.7.2.16 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.007.0002.html) and read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/new_mexico/ibc-2021/chapter/8/interior-finishes). Checked 2026-11-24.

- New Mexico's stall rules beyond the federal ones: [14.7.2.19, 14.7.2.44 and 14.7.2.45 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.007.0002.html) (Chapter 11, Appendix E with Table E111, baby changing facilities), ICC A117.1-2017 Sections 604.5.1 and 604.9.5 (read on a [secondary copy](https://up.codes/viewer/new_mexico/icc-a117.1-2017/chapter/6/plumbing-elements-and-facilities)) and the [2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design](https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/design-standards/2010-stds/), Sections 213.3.1, 604.5.1 and 604.8.1.4. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Restroom rules: [Gender-Free Restrooms Act, Laws 2019, House Bill 388](https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/19%20Regular/final/HB0388.PDF); [Human Rights Act amendments, Laws 2023, House Bill 207](https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/23%20Regular/final/HB0207.pdf); Section 2902.1.1 of the 2021 International Building Code as kept by [14.7.2.37 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.007.0002.html). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Public jobs: [11.1.2 NMAC, Public Works Minimum Wage Act Policy Manual](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title11/11.001.0002.html) (sections 11.1.2.8, 11.1.2.9 and 11.1.2.20), under the Public Works Minimum Wage Act, NMSA 1978, Sections 13-4-11 to 13-4-17. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Gross receipts tax: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department, [FYI-105, Gross Receipts & Compensating Taxes: An Overview](https://realfile.tax.newmexico.gov/FYI-105.pdf), [FYI-200, Gross Receipts Reporting Location and the Appropriate Tax Rate](https://realfile.tax.newmexico.gov/FYI-200.pdf), [FYI-206, Gross Receipts Tax and Marketplace Sales](https://realfile.tax.newmexico.gov/FYI-206.pdf), its [gross receipts tax overview](https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/businesses/gross-receipts-tax-overview/) and [3.2.1.15 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title03/03.002.0001.html) on delivery and freight charges. Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2017 as referenced by Chapter 11 and Appendix E of the 2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code (14.7.2 NMAC, the 2021 International Building Code with New Mexico amendments); 2024 New Mexico Plumbing Code (14.8.2 NMAC, the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code with New Mexico amendments; the 2021 edition may be used for permits until January 1, 2027); NFPA 286 for HDPE.

to_confirm: Small businesses and one shared restroom: 14.7.2.37 NMAC keeps only Sections 2901, 2902.1, Table 2902.1 and 2902.1.1 of IBC Chapter 29, and the plumbing code deletes the UPC's separate-facilities section. Ask the Construction Industries Division (CID) whether the model exceptions in IBC 2902.2 (15 or fewer occupants; offices of 25 or fewer) are applied, and whether IBC 2902.1.2 and 2902.4 (signs) are treated as in force.
Urinals: the state sentence says 'maximum number of water closets' and gives no rounding rule. Ask CID or local plan review how 50% and 67% are rounded on odd counts (the examples round down).
Table 2902.1 rows, Section 2902.1.1, Section 803.9, Table 1004.5, Section 1110.2.4 and ICC A117.1-2017 were read on UpCodes, not on the ICC's own site. Browser check before launch.
Which ICC A117.1 edition CID treats as 'the current adopted' one (the rule cites 2017 elsewhere).
Whether Albuquerque enforces these state rules unchanged (city agent).

2026 prevailing wage rates: the NMAC copy read still showed 2025 rates (Type B carpenter 30.89 + 13.26 fringe + .60 apprenticeship). Get the current Type B rate for Bernalillo County from the Department of Workforce Solutions, Labor Relations Division (the search result gave (505) 841-4400 and public.works@dws.nm.gov; not verified on the agency's own page).

Public Works Minimum Wage Act: statute text (NMSA 1978, Section 13-4-11) not opened; the $60,000 threshold comes from the rule. Two 2025 bills (SB 59, HB 6) touching the act appeared in search results; whether they passed was not checked.

State gross receipts tax rate 4.875%: from the FYI-105 edition dated July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, still the posted file on 2026-11-24. Confirm no change on July 1, 2026 with the Taxation and Revenue Department.

Gender-Free Restrooms Act: read as the enrolled bill; the codified section numbers (28-24-1 to 28-24-3) come from search results only. No statute restricting restroom use was found, but the compiled statutes were not searched in full.
Whether the Governor's Commission on Disability or another state body reviews plans for accessibility on state-funded projects (not read).
